content: Fluconazole, marketed under the brand name DIFLUCAN®, is the first member of a novel subclass of synthetic triazole antifungal agents. It is available in two forms for administration: oral tablets and a powder for oral suspension. Fluconazole is a white crystalline solid that exhibits slight solubility in water and saline solutions. DIFLUCAN tablets are manufactured in dosages of 50 mg, 100 mg, 150 mg, or 200 mg of fluconazole. These tablets also contain the following inactive ingredients: microcrystalline cellulose, dibasic calcium phosphate anhydrous, povidone, croscarmellose sodium, FD&C Red No. 40 aluminum lake dye, and magnesium stearate. The oral suspension form of DIFLUCAN is available in two strengths, containing either 350 mg or 1400 mg of fluconazole. The inactive ingredients in the suspension include sucrose, sodium citrate dihydrate, citric acid anhydrous, sodium benzoate, titanium dioxide, colloidal silicon dioxide, xanthan gum, and natural orange flavor. To prepare the oral suspension, the powder must be reconstituted with 24 mL of distilled water or Purified Water (USP). Once reconstituted, each milliliter of the suspension delivers either 10 mg or 40 mg of fluconazole, depending on the formulation.
